books.author: Ben Lerner
books.synopsis: A young Brooklyn poet and novelist, newly signed to a lucrative book deal and diagnosed with a dilated aorta, drifts through a New York bracing for a hurricane while he agrees to father a child for his best friend. A meditative, autofictional novel about time, art, mortality and literary fraud.

books.title: A Brief History of Seven Killings
books.author: Marlon James
books.synopsis: A polyphonic, multi-decade novel built around the 1976 attempted assassination of a reggae superstar known as the Singer in Kingston, Jamaica. Gang leaders, CIA operatives, a Rolling Stone journalist, and ordinary Jamaicans narrate the events and their fallout through the 1991 crack-era New York.

books.title: A Life's Work
books.author: Rachel Cusk
books.synopsis: Novelist Rachel Cusk gives a frank, unsentimental account of pregnancy, birth and the first year of her daughter's life, from colic and sleepless nights to the loss of her former self. Interweaving readings of novels and childcare manuals, it is a landmark of the modern motherhood memoir.

books.title: Aftermath
books.author: Rachel Cusk
books.synopsis: Rachel Cusk's memoir of her marriage breaking down and the disorienting life that follows for her and her two young daughters. She reads her own separation through Greek tragedy, writing about family, authority and the self in the wreckage of a household.

books.title: Agrippa
books.author: Robert Harris
books.synopsis: Told as the secret memoir of Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa, born feet-first and nicknamed the mother-killer, who becomes the commoner general and right-hand man of Octavius, the future Augustus. It follows the two friends from Caesar's assassination through the civil wars and the fall of the Republic.

books.title: Angle of Yaw
books.author: Ben Lerner
books.synopsis: Ben Lerner's second poetry collection, in five sections, mixing prose-poem and fragmentary lyric to interrogate sports, war, politics, the novel and the page itself. It closes with a Twenty-One Gun Salute for Ronald Reagan.

books.title: Another America
books.author: Barbara Kingsolver
books.synopsis: Barbara Kingsolver's poetry collection, in five sections, about injustice, exile, violence and endurance in the United States and the Americas. This bilingual edition pairs each poem with a Spanish translation by Rebeca Cartes.

books.title: Artful
books.author: Ali Smith
books.synopsis: Four Oxford lectures on time, form, edge, and offer and reflection, reworked by Ali Smith into a hybrid of essay and fiction. A grieving narrator reads her late partner's unfinished lectures on books, poems, and art, and the two voices slowly merge into one conversation about how stories work.

books.title: Babel
books.author: R. F. Kuang
books.synopsis: In an alternate 1830s Britain powered by silver-working, a Cantonese orphan is brought to Oxford to train at the Royal Institute of Translation, known as Babel, where magic is made from the gaps between languages. As he learns that the empire's wealth rests on colonial exploitation, he must choose between the institution that raised him and a secret society resisting it.

books.title: The Lacuna
books.author: Barbara Kingsolver
books.synopsis: Born to an American father and Mexican mother, Harrison Shepherd grows up between Mexico and the United States, and finds work as a plaster-mixer and cook in the household of Diego Rivera and Frida Kahlo, where he also becomes secretary to the exiled Leon Trotsky. Told through his notebooks and the papers of his archivist, the novel follows his later life as a reclusive novelist in North Carolina, caught up in the anti-Communist hysteria of the postwar years.

books.title: Black Leopard, Red Wolf
books.author: Marlon James
books.synopsis: In a mythic, pre-colonial Africa, a mercenary known as Tracker, who can smell anyone's trail, is hired to find a missing boy and joins a band of misfits that includes a shape-shifting Leopard. Narrated to an inquisitor from a prison cell, the first book of the Dark Star trilogy turns the hunt into a tangled and violent account of kingdoms, witches and monsters.

books.title: Companion Piece
books.author: Ali Smith
books.synopsis: During the pandemic lockdown, a lockdown-era academic who layer-paints the words of poems looks after her ailing father while a phone call from a near-stranger and two young girls, one obsessed with the Cottingley Fairies, upend her isolation. Folk tales of a smith, a curfew and a curlew cross with her own story as Smith explores real versus fake and the stories we inherit.

books.title: Coventry
books.author: Rachel Cusk
books.synopsis: A collection of essays by the novelist Rachel Cusk, gathering personal pieces on driving, rudeness, motherhood, family and home alongside criticism of art and literature. The final section turns to classics and bestsellers, with essays on Edith Wharton, D. H. Lawrence, Olivia Manning, Natalia Ginzburg, Kazuo Ishiguro and others.

books.title: Crossing the Wine-Dark Sea
books.author: Emily Wilson
books.synopsis: A collection of essays by the classicist and translator of the Odyssey and the Iliad on Greek and Roman literature and the art of translating it. Topics include Sappho, Aristophanes, Roman comedy, Helen of Troy, the Stoics, Christopher Logue's War Music, Edith Hamilton, and the problems of rendering Homer into English.

books.title: Small Wonder
books.author: Barbara Kingsolver
books.synopsis: A collection of twenty-three essays written in the wake of September 11, ranging from a Grand Canyon meditation and a defense of forests and seeds to letters to a daughter and a mother. Kingsolver weighs wonder, family, food, storytelling and what it means to love a country while grieving and questioning it.

books.title: Flight Behavior
books.author: Barbara Kingsolver
books.synopsis: Dellarobia Turnbow, a restless young farm wife in rural Tennessee, climbs a mountain intending to throw her life away and instead finds the forest ablaze with millions of monarch butterflies that have wintered in the wrong place. As scientists, reporters and a skeptical congregation descend on her family's land, her marriage, faith and sense of the future are all put to the test.

books.title: Girl Meets Boy
books.author: Ali Smith
books.synopsis: A retelling of Ovid's myth of Iphis set in contemporary Inverness, narrated alternately by two sisters, Midge and Imogen. While Imogen works at a corporation that bottles and sells Scottish water, a charismatic graffiti artist turns both sisters' lives upside down.

books.title: Glorious Exploits
books.author: Ferdia Lennon
books.synopsis: In Syracuse in 412 BC, two unemployed potters, Lampo and Gelon, decide to stage Euripides with the starving Athenian prisoners left to die in the city's quarries, trading scraps of food for recited lines. What starts as an eccentric scheme grows into an ambitious production that draws in the prisoners, the guards, and the whole divided city.

books.title: Glyph
books.author: Ali Smith
books.synopsis: A family story about a young man and a gassed, blinded horse in the First World War is passed down through generations and resurfaces in the present, when a sibling's bedroom is visited by what seems to be a ghost horse. The narrators search the internet, history and their own memories to work out what, if anything, the inherited story is really about.

books.title: How to be both
books.author: Ali Smith
books.synopsis: A two-part novel that can be read in either order: in one half, the spirit of a fifteenth-century Ferrarese painter, Francesco del Cossa, looks back on a life spent disguised as a boy to paint; in the other, a modern teenager, George, grieves her mother and becomes fascinated by a fresco in Italy. The halves echo and refract each other on art, gender, time and loss.

books.title: In the Fold
books.author: Rachel Cusk
books.synopsis: A young man from a modest background becomes entranced by the wealthy, chaotic Hanbury family of a country house called Egypt, and years later, married with a son, he finds the old pull of their world reasserting itself. A comedy of class, envy and domestic disillusionment.

books.title: Kudos
books.author: Rachel Cusk
books.synopsis: The writer Faye travels to a literary festival in Europe and passes through a series of encounters with publishers, interviewers and fellow passengers who talk at length about their lives. The final novel of the Outline trilogy, told almost entirely through what others confide to her.

books.title: Like
books.author: Ali Smith
books.synopsis: Two timelines intertwine: a mother and her young daughter Kate living in a seaside caravan, and Amy and Ash, two girls whose intense friendship begins in a small Scottish town. Ali Smith's debut novel circles loss, desire and the missing person at the heart of both stories.

books.title: Mean Free Path
books.author: Ben Lerner
books.synopsis: A book of poems in two linked sequences, 'Mean Free Path' and 'Doppler Elegies', that fold elegy, ambient media and political dread into fragmented, self-interrupting lines. Dedicated to Ari, it plays with reference, grief and the distance between speaker and subject.

books.title: Moon Witch, Spider King
books.author: Marlon James
books.synopsis: Second book of the Dark Star trilogy, told by the witch Sogolon, who recounts her own version of the events in Black Leopard, Red Wolf. From a childhood of abuse to a career as a spy and assassin at the court of the Kwash kings, she exposes what the Tracker's account left out.

books.title: Outline
books.author: Rachel Cusk
books.synopsis: A writer flies to Athens to teach a short creative-writing course and, over the following days, listens as seatmates, students, friends and fellow writers recount their marriages, regrets and self-deceptions. The narrator stays largely in outline while the stories of others fill the book.

books.title: Parade
books.author: Rachel Cusk
books.synopsis: Four linked stories (The Stuntman, The Midwife, The Diver, The Spy) circle artists and the marriages, families and reputations around them, beginning with a painter known only as G who starts painting upside down. The book is told in Cusk's detached, fable-like register.

books.title: Partita
books.author: Barbara Kingsolver
books.synopsis: Livia, a gifted young pianist from a Southern dairy-farm community, is haunted by her brother's death on the railroad tracks and by the question of how he could do it. Structured like a Bach partita, the novel follows her through conservatory ambition, a doomed love affair, injury, and a return to the farm and the neighbors she left.

books.title: Saving Agnes
books.author: Rachel Cusk
books.synopsis: Agnes Day, a recent English graduate, drifts through a shabby London of flatshares, dead-end temp jobs and unreliable love, trying to work out who she is supposed to be. Her housemates and a succession of lovers keep pulling her in different directions as she searches for a stable sense of self. Cusk's first novel is a comic portrait of early adulthood in the early 1990s.

books.title: The Accidental
books.author: Ali Smith
books.synopsis: The Smart family, on holiday in a rented house in Norfolk, is thrown into disarray when a stranger named Amber walks in and is taken for a colleague by each of them. The novel moves between the voices of the mother, stepfather, teenage son and young daughter, and of Amber herself.

books.title: The Country Life
books.author: Rachel Cusk
books.synopsis: Stella Benson, a lonely young woman escaping a failed London life, takes a job caring for a disabled teenage boy on a Sussex farm owned by the overbearing Maddens. Her letters, observations and awkward encounters with the household and village slowly unsettle the pastoral promise of country life. The novel is a comic, darkening riff on Jane Eyre and the English rural idyll.

books.title: The Devotion of Suspect X
books.author: Keigo Higashino
books.synopsis: In Tokyo, a brilliant but reclusive high-school math teacher, Ishigami, moves to shield his neighbor Yasuko Hanaoka after her abusive ex-husband turns up dead. Detective Kusanagi investigates and turns for help to his friend, the physicist Manabu Yukawa, who was Ishigami's university rival.

books.title: The Disappearers
books.author: Marlon James
books.synopsis: In 1988 Kingston, a group of men mount a staging of John Herbert's prison play Fortune and Men's Eyes, and the production ends in violence and a series of disappearances. The novel follows the survivors through journals, interview transcripts and letters across 1988, 1994, 1999 and 2005, from Jamaica to Miami and back.

books.title: The Last Supper
books.author: Rachel Cusk
books.synopsis: Rachel Cusk's account of a summer spent in Italy with her husband and two small children, travelling through Tuscany, Umbria, Rome and the south in search of art, food and a sense of home. Structured around the paintings of Piero della Francesca, Giotto and Raphael, it mixes travel writing with reflections on family life, motherhood and the writer's own restlessness.

books.title: The Lichtenberg Figures
books.author: Ben Lerner
books.synopsis: Ben Lerner's debut collection, a sequence of unrhymed fourteen-line sonnets that fracture and recombine speech, cliche, political and domestic scenes. Winner of the Hayden Carruth Award, it takes its title from the branching patterns left by electrical discharge.

books.title: The Lights
books.author: Ben Lerner
books.synopsis: A collection of poems and prose poems by Ben Lerner, organized around light, night, grief, fatherhood and the ordinary and civic life of the present. Moving between lyric, essay and anecdote, it takes in museums, paintings, a residency and the speaker's daughters.

books.title: The Poisonwood Bible
books.author: Barbara Kingsolver
books.synopsis: In 1959 the Baptist missionary Nathan Price takes his wife and four daughters to the Belgian Congo, where his zeal collides with the culture around him and with the country's slide toward independence and upheaval. The story is told in the alternating voices of Orleanna Price and her daughters over the following three decades.

books.title: The Temporary
books.author: Rachel Cusk
books.synopsis: Francine Snaith, a young woman who believes herself marked out by destiny, takes temp work in London and meets Ralph, a man weighed down by his past and his unreliable father. Their relationship becomes a study of hope, self-deception and the gap between how people see themselves and how they are seen. Cusk's second novel.

books.title: The Topeka School
books.author: Ben Lerner
books.synopsis: Adam Gordon, a high-school debate champion in 1990s Topeka, Kansas, grows up among his parents' psychiatric community at the Foundation while navigating masculinity, speech and the threat of violence. The novel shifts among the perspectives of Adam, his psychologist mother Jane and his father Jonathan, and later returns to Adam as an adult and father.

books.title: There but for the
books.author: Ali Smith
books.synopsis: At a dinner party in Greenwich, a guest named Miles Garth goes upstairs, locks himself in the spare room and refuses to come out. Four linked sections follow different people drawn into his orbit, among them a ten-year-old girl with a gift for wordplay, as the novel plays on language, history and the idea of belonging.

books.title: Transcription
books.author: Ben Lerner
books.synopsis: A writer on his way to interview Thomas, his ninety-year-old former teacher and a towering translator and thinker, drifts between recorded talks, memory, family life and the fragile business of turning speech into text. The narrator's pandemic-era care for his young daughter and his time in Providence, Madrid and a hotel on the French-Swiss border shape a meditation on mentorship, listening and mediation.

books.title: Transit
books.author: Rachel Cusk
books.synopsis: In the wake of her marriage's collapse, a writer moves with her two young sons to London and begins renovating a flat. Through a series of conversations with builders, hairdressers, fellow writers, old friends and a former lover, the story builds a quiet portrait of change, vulnerability and fate. It is the second novel in Cusk's Outline trilogy.

books.title: Unsheltered
books.author: Barbara Kingsolver
books.synopsis: Willa Knox inherits a crumbling house in Vineland, New Jersey, and tries to hold together her family amid a collapsing economy and a fraught new baby. A century and a half earlier, in the same town, the science teacher Thatcher Greenwood defends Darwin's ideas against a hostile community, with help from the naturalist Mary Treat. The two timelines echo each other across eras of upheaval.

books.title: Whistler
books.author: Ann Patchett
books.synopsis: Daphne, a high-school English teacher in New York, is shadowed through the Metropolitan Museum by an old man named Eddie, whom she first met as a nine-year-old trapped with him in a snowbound crashed car. Moving between that childhood night and the present, the novel follows her complicated family, her mother and stepfather, her sister Leda, and the long bond with the man who once edited novels.

books.title: Winter
books.author: Ali Smith
books.synopsis: On Christmas Eve, the semi-retired Sophia Cleves sees a disembodied child's head floating in her large, cold house in Cornwall. Her son Art, a nature blogger, hires a stranger named Lux to pose as his girlfriend for the holiday, and the group is joined by Sophia's estranged sister Iris, a veteran of the Greenham Common protests. The second of Smith's Seasonal quartet, it plays with ghosts, politics and the legacy of art.

books.title: Yellowface
books.author: Rebecca F. Kuang
books.synopsis: June Hayward, a struggling white novelist, watches her more successful Chinese American rival Athena Liu die in an accident and walks away with Athena's unpublished manuscript about Chinese laborers in World War I. She submits it as her own under an ambiguous pen name, and a satire of the publishing industry unfolds as her bestselling success becomes threatened by accusations of plagiarism and cultural appropriation.

books.title: Spring
books.author: Ali Smith
books.synopsis: Third of the Seasonal quartet, set in a Brexit-era Britain of detention centres and shrinking hope. A grieving screenwriter, a worn-down detention-centre guard and a mysterious girl on a train are drawn together, with Katherine Mansfield and Rainer Maria Rilke threaded through the story. (Source PDF is the Dutch translation, Lente.)
